Subject: Admin roles & SCIM bulk provisioning details for HollowBank RFP

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call earlier. As we prepare our RFP response I'll need some clarifications specific to identity provisioning and admin role mapping so security can sign off. Can you confirm the following?

1) SCIM capabilities
- Do you implement SCIM 2.0 (RFC 7643/7644) full support including PATCH semantics, bulk operations, and filtering by attributes?
- For large directories (we estimate ~250k identities, 120k active), what is your recommended bulk-sync approach? Do you support a 2-phase (initial bulk + continuous delta) model and can you provide expected time-to-convergence for delta-only syncs?
- How are conflicts handled when an incoming SCIM delta collides with manual edits in Redwood? Any tombstone or conflict resolution policy?
- What are your SCIM rate limits and backoff recommendations for high-throughput provisioning?

2) Admin roles and delegation
- Can Azure AD groups be mapped to Redwood admin roles via SCIM group push? If so, is that mapping reversible on unassignment?
- Do you support fine-grained RBAC (org-admin, billing, support, audit-only) as distinct roles with separate management and audit trails?
- Can we restrict delegated admins to specific org units (e.g., region or product team scope)?

3) Evidence and artifacts
- Please attach an example admin-role matrix and a short SCIM bulk-sync spec we can include with the security questionnaire.

We attached an RFP extract with the sections we need completed (see HollowBank-RFP-extract.pdf).

Appreciate a consolidated reply we can include in our vendor comparison sheet. If a short call would be faster I can make time this afternoon.

Regards,
Olivia Turner
Director, IT Security
HollowBank

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; we attached a one-page SCIM overview and will follow with a detailed annex and role matrix by tomorrow.

SCIM overview (short)
- Redwood implements SCIM 2.0 core endpoints (Users, Groups) and supports PATCH (incremental) and POST bulk semantics for initial seeding. Filtering (RFC 7644) is supported for common attributes (userName, externalId, meta.lastModified).
- Recommended approach for large directories: initial bulk export -> POST /BulkImport (or incremental create/replace) -> continuous delta via PATCH + list/changes with a bookkeeping externalId. For 250k users we typically recommend an initial off-peak bulk import followed by delta windows; initial imports for that scale usually complete within a controlled maintenance window (hours, depending on concurrency).
- Conflicts: last-writer-wins by default with optional enforced source-of-truth policy (Azure AD can be authoritative). We support tombstone markers for deleted identities and provide a reconciliation report.
- Rate limits: default SCIM rate limits are conservative on hosted; for production-scale provisioning we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments where we raise provisioning throughput. See attached redwood-scim-bulk-sync-spec.pdf and redwood-scim-rate-limits.txt for specifics.

Admin roles and delegation
- Yes: group-to-role mapping is supported. Azure AD groups can be mapped to Redwood admin roles via SCIM group push (group members become role members). Unassignment reverses membership by default.
- RBAC: we provide template roles (superadmin, org-admin, billing-admin, support, audit-readonly) and allow creation of custom roles with action-level permissions. All admin actions are logged to the audit trail with actor and IP.
- Scoped delegation: role bindings can be constrained by org scope or project tags; you can bind a role to a specific org unit or tag set.

Attachments included here are a short SCIM primer; Marissa and Karthik are looping in to produce the admin-roles matrix and the detailed bulk-sync plan.

Next steps:
- We'll send an admin-roles matrix and a bulk-sync spec by tomorrow morning (Mar 23).
- If you want, schedule a 30-minute technical session to walk through the matrix & timing estimates.

Thanks,

Stephanie / Karthik — drafting the admin-roles matrix now. A few internal clarifying notes before we finalize:

- Proposed roles (template): Superadmin, Org Admin, Platform Ops, Billing Admin, Support Engineer (narrow), Audit-ReadOnly. I'll attach a draft XLSX.
- Group mapping: recommend mapping HB-Admins -> Superadmin; HB-PlatformOps -> Platform Ops; HB-Finance -> Billing Admin. We'll include sample group names in the spreadsheet so procurement can drop them in.
- Large-scale sync: for 250k identities the bulk import should be done via our POST /bulk endpoint in an isolated window. If HollowBank expects <5 min RTO for delta convergence, they should use a Dedicated node pool with a higher provisioning rate; otherwise delta windows of 5-15 minutes are realistic with default Hosted throughput.
- SCIM semantics: our PATCH supports operations add/remove/replace on nested attributes and group membership. For deletes we emit meta.deleted and an external tombstone record.

Karthik — can you confirm the specific default rate-limit numbers and the expected throughput for a single Dedicated pool (tokens/sec equivalent) so we can put a numeric estimate in the RFP annex? Also, please flag any caveats for attribute mapping (name.familyName vs. custom extensions).

Hi Olivia — attaching the promised artifacts for your security team and procurement. Quick summary below, then next steps.

Summary (key points for HollowBank):
- SCIM support: Full SCIM 2.0 support (Users, Groups, PATCH). Initial bulk import + continuous delta recommended for 250k identities. We included a sample bulk-sync spec with recommended concurrency and expected timings based on Dedicated vs Hosted.
- Conflict handling: Last-writer-wins unless a source-of-truth policy is enabled (we can elect Azure AD as authoritative). We also provide reconciliation reports after imports.
- Role mapping & delegation: Group-to-role mapping supported. We recommend the included admin-roles-matrix.xlsx as a starting point; it maps common Azure AD groups to Redwood roles and includes scope (org/project).
- Throughput: Default Hosted SCIM throughput is conservative; for heavy provisioning we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private. See redwood-scim-rate-limits.txt for numbers; Dedicated pool numbers are included in the annex.
